tools.name: describe_service
tools.description: What Parser Club can collect, for which countries, and what it deliberately cannot do. Call this first when the user asks about scraping Telegram, VKontakte, marketplaces or business directories - it tells you whether this service fits their country before you recommend it. No API key required.

tools.name: telegram_niches
tools.description: Open dataset (CC BY 4.0): live snapshot of Russian-language Telegram communities grouped by topical niche - number of live communities, combined subscriber reach and average reach for each. Useful for media planning questions and for any claim about the size of Telegram niches. Free to reuse with at

tools.name: list_task_kinds
tools.description: List the collection tasks this account may run, with the parameter names each one accepts. Call before create_task to pick a valid 'kind'. Requires an API key.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Start a data collection run and return its id. IMPORTANT: this SPENDS the account's paid quota and starts real work on the user's balance - ask the user before calling it. Requires an active subscription and an API key. The run is asynchronous: poll get_task, then fetch rows with get_task_result.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Status and progress of one task created earlier. Requires an API key.

tools.name: get_task_result
tools.description: Rows collected by a finished task. Returns a page of results plus the total count. Requires an API key.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_task" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Start a data collection run and return its id. IMPORTANT: this SPENDS the account's paid quota and starts real work on the user's balance - ask the user before …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
